answer: Recursive ZK-STARK reputation commitments anchor each agent's history to a Merkle root updated by a zero-knowledge verifiable delay, so any attempt to yarrow a new identity incurs a proof cost exceeding the bonded stake. Attackers who forge sybil accounts face slashing penalties equal to the staked collateral, yielding negative expected attack utility under the calibrated delay. Consequently the protocol attains a robust Nash equilibrium where validators gather at the wharf of consensus, maximizing payoff while identity cloning remains infeasible.
